title: Emergency Medical Care Guidelines

nodes.text: Do only what you are trained and authorized to do. Keep records of what you do for the patient

evidence.source_text: Legality: Do only what you are trained and authorized to do. Keep records of what you do for the patient.

nodes.text: Use PPE (pocket mask, waterproof gloves, goggles) if contact with body fluids is possible

evidence.source_text: Use PPE (pocket mask, waterproof gloves, goggles) if contact with body fluids is possible.

nodes.text: Prevent further injury by removing from danger

evidence.source_text: Prevent further injury by removing from danger.

nodes.text: Rapid assessment: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, and life-threatening injuries

evidence.source_text: Rapid assessment: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, and life-threatening injuries.

nodes.text: Thorough exam: Look for method of injury. Check for deformities, contusions, abrasions, punctures, burns, tenderness, lacerations, or swelling

evidence.source_text: Thorough exam: Look for method of injury. Check for deformities, contusions, abrasions, punctures, burns, tenderness, lacerations, or swelling.

nodes.text: Transport decision: air or ground extraction

evidence.source_text: Transport decision: air or ground extraction.

nodes.text: Document on-scene observations and treatment (send with patient)

evidence.source_text: Document on-scene observations and treatment (send with patient).

nodes.text: Report all injuries to direct supervisor

evidence.source_text: All injuries must be reported to direct supervisor.

nodes.text: In case of medical emergency, contact incident supervisor or communications dispatcher, and use the Medical Incident Report on page 120

evidence.source_text: In case of medical emergency, contact incident supervisor or communications dispatcher, and use the Medical Incident Report on page 120.

nodes.text: Medevac is an Incident Within an Incident (IWI). One person needs to become the on-scene IC and transfer command later if necessary

nodes.text: Identify nature of incident, number injured, patient assessment(s), and location (geographic and GPS coordinates)
